say.en: "Ravi is 165 centimetres tall" is a number. "The average height of our class is 162 centimetres" is also a number. Only one of them is statistics. Which one, and why? In this lesson: Quote the definitions of Bowley, Croxton and Cowden and Secrist.
List the characteristics of statistics.
Decide whether given facts are statistics.

body.en: Bowley: "*Statistics* may be called the science of counting" and "the science of averages". Croxton and Cowden: "Statistics may be defined as the collection, presentation, analysis and interpretation of numerical data." R. A. Fisher saw statistics as mathematics applied to observational data. The Croxton and Cowden definition (singular sense) names the four stages of every statistical study.
body.kn: ಬೌಲೆ: "ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಎಣಿಕೆಯ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ", "ಸರಾಸರಿಗಳ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ". ಕ್ರಾಕ್ಸ್‌ಟನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕೌಡೆನ್: "ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣೆ, ನಿರೂಪಣೆ, ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನ" ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ. ಇದು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಹಂತಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Statistics are affected by many causes

narration.en: Secrist's characteristics: statistics are aggregates of facts, affected to a marked extent by a multiplicity of causes, numerically expressed, estimated with reasonable accuracy, collected systematically for a purpose and placed in relation to each other. The yield of paddy depends on rainfall, fertiliser and seed together (illustrative model): no single cause explains it.

problem.en: Which of these are statistics? (a) Ravi's height is 165 cm. (b) The heights of 50 students of a class. (c) Mysuru is a beautiful city. (d) The populations of Karnataka's districts in Census 2011.

steps.en: (a) is a single, isolated fact: not an aggregate.
(c) is a qualitative remark, not numerically expressed.
(b) and (d) are aggregates of numerical facts, collected for a purpose and comparable.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Which of these are statistics? a Ravi's height is 165 centimetres. b The heights of 50 students of a class. c Mysuru is a beautiful city. d The populations of Karnataka's districts in Census 2011.
a is a single, isolated fact: not an aggregate.
c is a qualitative remark, not numerically expressed.
b and d are aggregates of numerical facts, collected for a purpose and comparable.
So the answer is b and d are statistics.

say.en: Croxton and Cowden: collection, presentation, analysis, interpretation.
say.kn: ಕ್ರಾಕ್ಸ್‌ಟನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕೌಡೆನ್: ಸಂಗ್ರಹಣೆ, ನಿರೂಪಣೆ, ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ, ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನ.

say.en: Secrist: statistics are aggregates of facts, numerical and comparable.
say.kn: ಸೆಕ್ರಿಸ್ಟ್: ಅಂಕಿಅಂಶಗಳು ಸಂಗತಿಗಳ ಸಮೂಹ, ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ಮತ್ತು ಹೋಲಿಸಬಹುದಾದವು.

say.en: A single isolated figure is not statistics.
